text: Schools should push the start of the day back to 8:30. Dr. Lin's survey found that students sleeping at least eight hours scored 3.5 points higher on morning tests. Therefore one year group could trial the change and compare lateness and results.

Cities should add bus lanes, because buses carry more people yet are slowed by private traffic. Trialling two congested corridors and publishing travel times would show whether the policy is worth widening.

Schools should not ban phones across the whole campus. Collecting them during lessons cuts distraction, however students may need to reach family at lunch and after school. Comparing discipline records and emergency contacts before and after would show whether a wider limit is justified.

University canteens could offer half portions to cut waste. Fixed portions leave smaller eaters with food on the plate, whereas half portions let students take what they need. The canteen should record sales and leftovers for each size, and widen the menu only if total waste falls at an acceptable cost.

Companies could let staff work remotely two days a week. Remote days cut commuting time, although some collaborative work is still better done face to face. One team should trial it for three months and compare delivery speed, defect rates and staff feedback before any long-term policy.
